vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security updates - immediate, high priority. This must be the top-level vulnerabilityAlerts object, which applies only to updates that fix a known vulnerability: as a packageRule matching every package it labelled every update security/urgent, titled it fix(security) and dropped its schedule and release-age wait (PR #154 was a plain Go minor bump).

schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Testing libraries - safe automerge for patches

GitHub Actions - major updates: automerge after a 14-day soak once CI passes. Actions are SHA-pinned and gated by the full PR CI (lint/test/e2e/build); only release.yml-exclusive actions aren't exercised by PR CI, so watch the first release after a docker/* action major.

Dockerfile's golang base image tag is not an independent dependency: it must equal pkg/versions/dependencies.yaml's go_version (enforced in CI by scripts/check-go-version, see .github/workflows/go-version.yml). Disable the built-in dockerfile manager for it so Renovate stops proposing it on its own datasource/schedule (e.g. PR #151) - the customManager below tracks it together with go_version instead, in one PR.

lint.yml's golangci-lint `version:` input is one of four pins of the same version. The built-in github-actions manager would bump it alone; disable that so the golangci-lint customManager below bumps all four together in one PR.

The `go` directive of this repo's go.mod files is not an independent dependency either: the go-version customManager below bumps it with go_version and the Dockerfile. Disable the gomod manager's own proposal for it (it would bump go.mod alone).

The Go version's four pins share one rule, so they get one release-age wait and land in one PR. Without it the provider-framework rule (matched by file name) took go_version into its group with a 7-day wait while the Dockerfile tag went alone with none, splitting one version into two PRs at two different versions (#154, #157). Patches get their own PR (separateMinorPatch), so declining a Go minor bump can never also block a security patch on the current minor.

Generated-provider framework deps (pkg/versions/dependencies.yaml) - bump together so crossplane-runtime, crossplane/apis, controller-runtime, and k8s.io/* stay mutually compatible (individual bumps break the e2e)

Never propose upjet/v2 v2.4.0 or older: released v2.4.0 imports crossplane-runtime/v2/apis/common/v1, which crossplane-runtime removed in its own v2.4.0, so make generate fails in a scaffolded upjet provider. upjet was once pinned to a post-v2.4.0 pseudo-version for this, and with rollbackPrs enabled Renovate proposed v2.4.0 as a 'rollback' (PRs #134, #152). The pin is a release (v2.5.1) now; the floor stays so a rollback can never be proposed again.

customManagers.description: Track generated-provider dependency versions in pkg/versions/dependencies.yaml

Track the Go version as ONE dependency across pkg/versions/dependencies.yaml's go_version, the Dockerfile's golang base image tag and the `go` directive of this repo's two go.mod files, so a bump proposes all four together in a single PR - never one alone (that drift is what broke five times in September). scripts/check-go-version fails CI if any of them disagree.

Track golangci-lint as ONE dependency across the four places that pin it - this repo's Makefile, lint.yml's golangci-lint-action `version:` input, and both flavors' generated make fragment - so a bump proposes all four in a single PR. hack/check-consistency.sh (C10) fails CI if they ever disagree.

Track the git-cliff release version release.yml installs from GitHub releases as a pinned binary (deliberately not orhun/git-cliff-action, see release.yml's comment). The action's own `uses:` SHA is tracked separately by helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests.

Track the GoReleaser version goreleaser-action's `version:` input pins in release.yml - a floating input Renovate does not follow on its own (the action's `uses:` SHA is tracked separately by helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests).
